chapter: C.L. Burke and Kid Ory years
title: Steady work, credit and buying his first home
summary: A long steady job let him obtain credit and buy a home in Willowbrook, which he sold decades later.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Musicians went on jobs and worked for a long time like that, in those times, if they had a good gig; they spent several years there, unlike the later two weeks here and four weeks here.
That's right. I liked it because I wanted a steady job.
Right; take care of your family.
I was able to get good credit too being on a job for a long time. That's when I bought my first home.
Really? That's interesting because I'm sure it was difficult for musicians then, even more difficult than it is now for them to get credit.
It certainly was.
I have been told that oftentimes the club owners would vouch for a musician, to help them establish their cre-
dit and buy homes and so forth. I got credit on my own because I had been working at Bell Tavern well over a year when I applied for it.
And that's when you bought your first home?
That's right.
Do you remember where that home was? I bet you never forgot it.
Oh, sure. 121 17 Parmalee.
That was in the Watts area; wasn't it?
That's it. Willowbrook.
That's just a little east of the Watts area; isn't it?
A little south. 122nd and Parmalee. Imperial was the dividing line of Watts, and just below that was the
county, and Willowbrook started I think, around 118th Street.
That area still has some very comfortable homes.
I sold my home in 1940--no, '50.
You sold your home there in 1950?
It must have been '61.
